data.narrative:
ARC Clean Technology, a Series G nuclear energy company that has raised $50M+, operates within a sector comprised of 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 4 private competitors (Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy). This peer universe remains nascent and fragmented, limiting conventional benchmarking approaches.

The valuation analysis applied stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($50M) as a base proxy and applying a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical for Series G to subsequent-stage transitions, this method yields an implied value of $62M. Peer-median triangulation was not feasible: while four same-sector companies exist, none satisfied adjacent-stage or similar-valuation-tier filters necessary to establish a credible comparable set of three or more datapoints. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the specialized nature of nuclear technology development and capital requirements.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $53M to $72M, with a median estimate of $62M. This single-method basis reflects a material constraint: the nuclear energy sector lacks sufficient public-market or late-stage private comparables to anchor peer-based valuation. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to the named peer set, capital efficiency relative to sector burn rates, and path-to-commercialization timelines, none of which are quantified in available data. Further clarity on deployment timelines and unit economics would strengthen conviction in this range.
